text:
anne (Product): Quick sync — we need a decision on how to ship the new pricing behavior for high-throughput customers: create a standalone "Flex QoS" add-on (metered credits + burst window) or increase existing tier ceilings with rollover/grandfathering. Launch target: next month. Thoughts?

mike (BizOps): My +1 is for an add-on. Easier to SKU, simpler for forecasting. Avoids reshaping base tiers mid-quarter. :thinking:

liam (Sales): Add-on worries me for enterprise renewals. They hate new SKUs during negotiations. If we do add-on, we must offer a clear migration/discount path in contract. I can pilot with two accounts if we commit to a grandfather option.

reza (Eng): From implementation side, add-on = simpler flag + quota service change. We can route by org-header and apply burst windows without touching tier logic. Rough effort: 2 sprints (incl. tests). Need schema: 
```json
{"addon_id":"flex-qos","burst_window_seconds":300,"burst_tokens":200000,"daily_cap_tokens":2000000}
```

sophia (SRE): Operational constraints: don't allow unlimited bursts. Recommend default burst_window=300s, per-org daily_cap, and autopause if error rate > 1.5% during burst. Also require observability hooks (per-addon error & latency metrics).

anne (Product): Good. We still must decide pricing shape: flat monthly fee for addon vs token-based credits. Also list launch gating items I want before we flip the switch:
- docs + billing mappings
- console UI for enabling/disabling addon per org
- legal T&Cs + entitlements update
- migration playbook for existing customers (grandfather/grace period)
- canary + rollback plan (metrics and thresholds)

mike (BizOps): Proposal: dual SKU — small monthly access fee + metered credits. Access fee covers priority routing. Metered credits consumed only during burst above tier baseline. Easier to show value.

liam (Sales): Sample pricing I'd propose for pilot: $500/mo access + $0.30 per 1k tokens above baseline. For large customers we can negotiate commit discounts. I'll validate willingness to pay with pilot accounts this week.

reza (Eng): We need a canary toggle in runtime: allow addon on for <=5% of requests across 2 regions. Rollback if p95 latency increases > 25% or error rate > 1%. I'll add a feature flag and a metric dashboard.

sophia (SRE): Add to rollout checklist: synthetic load test (replicate 2x expected burst) and an automated throttle circuit that flips to safe-mode on anomalies. Otherwise we risk noisy neighbor effects.

anne (Product): OK owners:
- product: anne — finalize pricing shape & migration text
- bizops: mike — SKU definition + reporting mapping
- sales: liam — pilot customers + feedback
- eng: reza — feature flag + quota enforcement
- srep: sophia — auto-throttle & runbooks

ci-bot: deploy-bot: Canary featureflag 'flex-qos' created in staging. (build #4821) :rocket:

liam (Sales): I'll confirm pilot 3 customers by EOD Friday. If they accept the pilot price, we can ship beta to them next week.

mike (BizOps): I'll draft SKU docs and sample invoice mapping today, will post link here.

anne (Product): Final QA: if we see pilot customers using < 20% of burst capacity and NPS doesn't drop, greenlight GA. Otherwise iterate. Thanks everyone — will follow up with a short spec and timeline in this thread.
